pitch · sebthecanadian.ca — distilling what's already there
rev. 01 · apr 2026
From: A designer who read every file To: Seb (the Canadian) Re: front door, sharpened

Your site already knows
what it wants to be.

You’ve written the best design brief I’ve read in a while — Illich, the IndieWeb, a “data druid” aesthetic, durability over trend, human-scale tools. The problem isn’t the thinking. It’s that the page you land on doesn’t yet match the page you describe.

This pitch is a distillation, not a pivot. No new palette, no new stack, no React, no framework. Same tokens, same Eleventy build, same Plex Mono. The move is to quiet the decoration, commit to the monospace, earn the nav back down to four items, and stop pretending this is a blog. Make the front door feel like a front door.

read time ~ 8 minutes · scroll, or press J / K to jump sections

01Diagnosis

The site is quietly arguing with itself.

Four tensions, each between something the brief says and something the page does. Each is fixable without touching Eleventy or the content model.

Tension 01Form ≠ ethos

A “Caves of Qud data druid” on a stock markdown template.

“Low-fi authenticity. Terminal aesthetic. Dense information respects reader's time.”

Headings are monospace. Body copy is system-sans. Pixel banners appear on two pages, dividers on none of them, and the rest is a 68ch column of markdown. The aesthetic is being sprinkled, not committed to.

Tension 02Two faces

Two portraits, one person, no rule.

“Durable identity. Portable publishing. Clear ownership of work.”

There’s a woodcut stamp (warm, hand-made) and a pixel-art portrait (cool, game-like). Both are good. Neither has a defined role. The favicon is a third mark. Identity needs a system, not a library.

Tension 03Nav bloat

Eleven navigation destinations. One post.

“Make what you need. Don’t add complexity for hypothetical visitors.”

Primary: Home · Projects · Writing · Resume · Now · About. Secondary: Uses · Links · Garden · Email · RSS. Home/About/Now semantically overlap. Links is a three-line blogroll. You are what you link to — right now the site links to itself eleven times before it says hello.

Tension 04Hub vs. blog

Writing page promises the garden, then lists one native post above it.

“This page collects excerpts and syndication links — a hub, not a destination.”

The architecture is right; the visual weight is wrong. Hello, IndieWeb gets the same card treatment as the nine garden entries it’s supposed to be pointing toward. The reader can’t tell which is the body of work.

02Thesis

Commit to the low-fi, monospace, tended-garden voice you already named. Make every pixel carry its weight, or cut it.

PRINCIPLE · A

Same soul, sharper edges.

Keep the palette, the stack, the microformats, the “forest at night.” Remove everything that isn’t pulling weight: the sprinkled pixel art, the default markdown rhythm, the half-commitment to sans.

PRINCIPLE · B

The medium is the argument.

Illich + IndieWeb isn’t theme, it’s structure. A site about convivial tools should read like a convivial tool: dense, legible, forkable, quiet. Fully monospace. Generous whitespace. No animation that isn’t diegetic.

PRINCIPLE · C

Fewer doors, honest signs.

Four primary destinations. Clear contracts on each. The garden is a separate place — treat it like a neighbour, not a tenant.

03Five concrete moves

Small surface. Heavy leverage.

Each of these is a one- to three-hour change to files you already have. Taken together they change how the site feels on arrival without rewriting a single page.

Move 01 — Structure

Collapse the nav. Four doors, not eleven.

Home · Writing · Projects · Resume. Everything else lives in the footer as a colophon row, or one level deep. Now folds into Home (it’s already a single short list). About becomes Home’s lower half. Uses and Links go in the colophon. The garden gets a dedicated, clearly-external signpost — not a nav item pretending to be internal.

  • Primary reads as a path, not a menu: home · writing · projects · resume
  • Footer colophon absorbs uses / links / rss / contact / “this is how this site is built”
  • Garden is a first-class outbound link with a persistent live-tended timestamp
  • Now becomes a single block on home, tagged with “last tended” — fewer URLs to maintain

Move 02 — Typography

Go fully monospace. Let the grid do the work.

You’re already using IBM Plex Mono for headings and code. Use it for body too. Plex Mono is one of the most legible monospaces ever shipped — it was designed as a system font. At 15–16px with 1.6 line-height, it reads as comfortably as Atkinson Hyperlegible and signals the ethos on every line.

  • Body: IBM Plex Mono 400 · 15.5px / 1.62 · measure 64ch (down from 68)
  • Headings: same family, 600/700 · tighter tracking (-0.01em) · no size changes needed
  • Drop Google Fonts and Atkinson Hyperlegible entirely. You self-host Plex. One less request, one fewer faux-bold risk.
  • Kill the smooth scroll and view-transitions — they’re the opposite of the “works in text browsers” ethic

Move 03 — Home

Make the home page a front door, not a feed.

A front door says: this is who I am, here’s what I’m working on, here’s where to find the body of the work. Right now home is a hero, a garden promo, a single featured project, a single latest post, and a list of profile links. That’s a blog pretending not to be one. Replace the “Latest Writing” card with a living index.

  • One-liner identity — name, what I work on, city
  • Now block — three lines, timestamped “tended” (folds in /now/)
  • Index table — writing, projects, garden activity, each with a tended-date — terminal-style rows, not cards
  • Contact at the bottom. Email. Bluesky. GitHub. End of front door.

Move 04 — Palette

Keep the forest. Recalibrate for AA across both modes.

The palette is good. It just has two small problems: light-mode muted (#6b5d54, brown) and dark-mode muted (#a89eb8, purple-tinted) don’t share a tonal family, and the amber accent (#e9d66b) is too pale on parchment for anything smaller than 18pt. Small shifts, same vibe, real WCAG.

  • Moss deepens: #4a8c6f → #3f7a5f (light) · dark mode stays #6bb896 (lifted slightly)
  • Amber darkens on parchment: #e9d66b → #b07a0f · the bright #d9b24a stays for dark
  • Muted unifies: same neutral family both modes; no more brown/purple drift
  • One new role: --wash — a 6% moss tint, for the garden-feature panel only

Every pair meets AA 4.5:1 at body size. Moss and amber are semantic: moss = alive / internal / tended; amber = external / archive / warning.

Move 05 — Identity

One rule for the portrait. One rule for the mark.

Two portraits is fine — if each has a job. Proposal: the woodcut stamp is the human-scale identity (home, about, resume, og:image). The pixel portrait is the system-scale identity (favicon source, og:image for posts, 404, inline tiny monogram). Never both on the same page. The monogram glyph retires from the favicon and returns as a recurring "section stamp" at the start of each page title block — two characters of ink where the pixel moss-divider used to be.

  • Woodcut stamp — about / resume / og:default · human, warm, dateable
  • Pixel portrait — favicon / og:writing / 404 · system, durable, scaleable
  • Monogram — inline glyph on section starts · ascii-simple, a quiet signature
  • Retire: banners, moss-dividers, the leaf-drift animation. They’re decoration pretending to be structure.

04Against your own principles

A pitch worth taking has to pass the tests in DESIGN_PRINCIPLES.md.

You wrote four gates: convivial · IndieWeb · sustainable · accessible. Here’s how this pitch scores against each — honestly, including where the trade-offs are.

Convivial

Pass. Fewer moving parts. CSS simplifies (~30% less). One font family instead of two. No animation library. Every component readable in a text browser. Fork-ability goes up, not down.

IndieWeb

Pass — with care. All microformats preserved (h-card, h-entry, h-feed, h-resume, u-photo). Webmentions untouched. Rel-me chain intact. One small addition: u-photo on the woodcut stamp is formalized, since right now only h-card is declared without the photo.

Sustainable

Strong pass. Zero new dependencies. One CSS file merges cleanly into your existing four. Still hand-editable. Still works on a Raspberry Pi. Removes Google Fonts, one CDN blast radius gone.

Accessible

Meaningful upgrade. All AA at body size (current amber fails). Fixes the IMPROVEMENT_AUDIT Batch 1 findings inline (A1–A5). Reduced-motion respected everywhere. Skip link, landmarks, focus rings preserved. New body measure (64ch) improves screen-reader line breaks too.

05How we ship it

Four afternoons. No framework change. No content migration.

Structured so you can stop at any step and still have a better site than you had before step 01. Each afternoon is its own PR.

06Where I’m holding back

The most important part of a pitch is what it refuses to do.

A bad redesigner would pitch you a dark hero, a big animated portrait, a cursor trail, and a Bluesky feed. Here’s an explicit fence around what’s in scope.

In scope · Yes
  • Tokens, type, nav, home, writing, identity rules
  • Fixing the audit's accessibility + performance findings in-line
  • One print stylesheet pass on resume
  • Documentation: one updated ADR-style note, nothing more
Out of scope · No
  • No framework change. Eleventy stays. Nunjucks stays.
  • No new fonts. Plex Mono only, self-hosted.
  • No JS beyond your existing three small files. Zero deps.
  • No CMS, no build-time image pipeline, no new data model.
  • No hand-drawn SVG illustration I didn’t already have source for.
  • No migration of garden content. That’s a different project.
07Close

The brief you wrote is the design. This pitch just reads it more carefully than the current build does.

I want to be your designer because I read every file. I noticed that now.md reads like a front door already. I noticed the garden excerpts have seed / seedling statuses that nobody on the home page ever gets to see. I noticed that the moss divider is driven by mask-image so it can be recolored — a beautiful detail nobody will ever open devtools to find.

A site like this is won on small decisions, compounded. Four afternoons. One voice. Same soul.
